title: A strictly standard nonzerodivisor from the field case
statement: Assume that every regular map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] $k\to L$ from a field to a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] has $L$ a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Let $R\to\Lambda$ be a regular map of Noetherian rings with $R$ reduced (every nilpotent element is zero) and nonzero. For every finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $R$-algebra map $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$, there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$, maps $a:A\to B$, $\beta:B\to\Lambda$, and a nonzerodivisor $\pi\in R$ (multiplication by $\pi$ is injective) such that $\beta a=\alpha$ and the image of $\pi$ in $B$ is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. $B$ lives in the common universe of $A$ and $\Lambda$, containing the universe of $R$.

proof.text: PT over the total ring of fractions. Let $S\subset R$ be the set of nonzerodivisors and $Q=S^{-1}R$. $R$ is reduced, Noetherian and nonzero, so it has finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], $t\ge1$ (a nonzero ring has a prime, and every prime contains a minimal prime), and by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] each $K_i=R_{\mathfrak q_i}=\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$ is a field and $Q\to K_1\times\cdots\times K_t$ is an isomorphism. Tensoring with $\Lambda$ over $R$: $S^{-1}\Lambda\cong\Lambda\otimes_RQ\cong\prod_i\Lambda\otimes_RK_i=:\prod_i\Lambda_i$ (localization is base change to $S^{-1}R$, and $\otimes$ commutes with finite products), compatibly with $Q\cong\prod_iK_i$. Each $\Lambda_i=\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is the fibre ring of $R\to\Lambda$ at $\mathfrak q_i$, so it is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)=K_i$ by regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Hence $K_i\to\Lambda_i$ is a regular ring map of Noetherian rings: it is flat, every module over a field being free [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and its only fibre ring, over the prime $(0)$ of $K_i$ with $\kappa((0))=K_i$, is $\Lambda_i\otimes_{K_i}K_i\cong\Lambda_i$. By the field-case hypothesis PT holds for each $K_i\to\Lambda_i$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-product], applied $t-1$ times ($(K_1\times\cdots\times K_{s})\times K_{s+1}$ for $s=1,\dots,t-1$), PT holds for $\prod_iK_i\to\prod_i\Lambda_i$, hence, transporting along the isomorphisms $Q\cong\prod_iK_i$, $S^{-1}\Lambda\cong\prod_i\Lambda_i$, for $Q\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), third paragraph ('Q = K_1 x ... x K_n is a product of fields, see Algebra, Lemmas 02LX and 00FR. By Lemma 07F3 and our assumption PT holds for S^{-1}R -> S^{-1}Lambda'; the regularity of K_i -> Lambda_i, which Stacks leaves implicit, is written out here)

proof.text: A smooth factorization over $Q$. $S^{-1}A\cong A\otimes_RQ$ is a $Q$-algebra of finite presentation (a presentation of $A$ over $R$ base-changes to one over $Q$), and $S^{-1}\alpha:S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ is a homomorphism of $Q$-algebras. By the preceding step, $S^{-1}\Lambda$ is a colimit, in the category of commutative $Q$-algebras, of a filtered diagram $j\mapsto B_j$ of smooth $Q$-algebras with coprojections $\iota_j$ [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]; by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) it is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] there are $j$ and a $Q$-algebra map $\beta':S^{-1}A\to B_j$ with $\iota_j\circ\beta'=S^{-1}\alpha$. Put $B'=B_j$, $\gamma'=\iota_j$: a factorization $S^{-1}A\to B'\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ of $S^{-1}\alpha$ with $B'$ smooth over $Q=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), third paragraph ('Hence we can find a factorization S^{-1}A -> B' -> S^{-1}Lambda with B' smooth over S^{-1}R', i.e. Algebra Lemma 07C3, (1) implies (2))

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-base] to the localized smooth factorization. This gives a finitely presented algebra $B$, maps $A\to B\to\Lambda$ with composite $\alpha$, and $\pi$ in the nonzerodivisor submonoid whose image is elementary standard. An elementary standard element is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]: use the coefficient of its initial minor for that subset of columns and zero for all other subsets; transpose the minor matrix if needed. The relation condition is unchanged. The delocalization constructs a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over $R$, hence its carrier is in the common universe of $A$ and $\Lambda$.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_standard_nonzerodivisor
    (h : ∀ (k : Type u) (Λ : Type (max u v)) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
      [IsNoetherianRing Λ],
      RingHom.IsRegular (algebraMap k Λ) →
        ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
          (fun B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} k ↦ Algebra.Smooth k B)
          (CommAlgCat.of k Λ))
    (R : Type u) (Λ : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Nontrivial R] [IsReduced R]
    (hreg : RingHom.IsRegular (algebraMap R Λ))
    (A : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (α : A →ₐ[R] Λ) :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B)
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R B) (aB : A →ₐ[R] B) (β : B →ₐ[R] Λ) (π : R),
      β.comp aB = α ∧ π ∈ R⁰ ∧
        Algebra.IsStrictlyStandardElement (R := R) (algebraMap R B π)
